title: This Is / That Is: Things Around You
objective: Name everyday objects and point to them with this and that; ask What's this?
intro_md:
[L1: In this lesson you learn words for things around you: pen, book, phone, bag, chair, table. You point to a thing NEAR you with "this" and to a thing FAR from you with "that": This is my phone. That is a chair. To ask about a thing, say "What's this?"]
{{l1_contrast:demonstratives_this_that}}
notes: TODO_audio: exercises 2 and 5 need recorded audio; the quoted text in the prompt stands in for the recording. Flashcards (exercise 1) need audio fronts. Coordination: 'new' (band item 43) was introduced by L07 ('new student'), so this lesson recycles it via vocabulary_refs; 'desk' from the band's classroom-object tail holds L14's allocation of 10 new items.

exercises.prompt: this · that · What's this? · pen · book · phone · bag · chair · table · desk
exercises.rationale: Form-meaning link for the six objects plus the this/that pair and the question chunk, with audio, before production.

exercises.prompt: [audio, 0.75x] 'What's this? — It's a pen.' — [L1: Which thing do they talk about?]
exercises.rationale: Comprehension of the answer slot after 'It's a'; trains hearing the object name inside the question-answer pair.

options.label: pen
options.rationale: Named after 'It's a' — the answer slot of What's this?

options.label: bag
options.rationale: Another taught object; forces word-level listening, not guessing.

options.label: this
options.rationale: Catches learners who match the question word instead of the answer.

exercises.prompt: [L1: Match the sentence to the situation.]

pairs.right: [L1: The phone is in my hand.]
[L1: The phone is across the room.]
[L1: You sit at the desk right now.]
[L1: You ask about a thing far from you.]

exercises.rationale: Anchors this/that to physical distance in context, not translation; adds What's that? as the far twin of the taught question chunk and deploys the new object desk in a near-situation.

exercises.prompt: [L1: The pen is in your hand.] ___ is a pen.
exercises.rationale: First forced distance choice from a situational cue; 'It' separates pointing (this/that) from referring back (it), a persistent A1 confusion.

exercises.prompt: [audio, 0.75x] 'That's a chair.' — [L1: What do you hear?]
exercises.rationale: The contracted 's in That's is quiet; zero-copula L1s (zh/ar/vi) systematically drop it — perception before production per the copula contrast note.

options.label: That's a chair.
options.rationale: That IS a chair — the 's is small but always there.

options.label: That a chair.
options.rationale: Missing 's. Zero-copula transfer (zh/ar/vi drop 'is' after this/that).

options.label: That's a table.
options.rationale: Wrong object; keeps word-level listening honest while the grammar is in focus.

exercises.prompt: [L1: The book is on your desk, near you.] A: What's ___?  B: It's ___ English book.
exercises.rationale: Integrates the new question chunk with L13's a/an: near cue forces 'this', vowel-initial English forces 'an' — 'a English' is a high-frequency A1 error.

exercises.prompt: [L1: Put the words in order to ask about a thing near you.]
exercises.rationale: Expands the chunk What's this? into its full form; predicted in-situ error 'This is what?' (zh transfer) — feedback names the fronted question word.
Adjective-before-noun order: es speakers say 'teléfono nuevo', so 'my phone new' is the predicted order — feedback names the adjective position.

exercises.prompt: [L1: Three questions start with What. Match each to its answer.]
exercises.rationale: All three unit questions begin with What — learners must attend past the first word to the frame. Recycles L03 (N-2) and L13.

exercises.prompt: [L1: Look around you. Tell the AI about three real things: two near you (this), one far (that). Then ask the AI about one thing.]
exercises.rationale: Real deixis with the learner's own environment; the AI checks this/that consistency with stated distance. Counts toward guided-interaction minutes.
